newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India rebound fuels overseas shares.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India rebound fuels overseas shares.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) rallied further on Friday, driven by a firmer trend on the domestic market.
"Things are going a bit better some of the blue chips are going a lot better. Premiums are looking happier," said a trader.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed up 1.53 points, 2.51 percent, at 62.39 points, with the premium over the local market at 11.22 percent after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index rose 34.18 points or 1.09 percent to 3,160.52.
"The market has a better feel about it. Some of the blue chips are going a lot better," said a trader.
Bajaj Auto added $1.30 to $31.00/$32.00, BSES was up 48 cents $16.25/$17.25 and Telco 75 cents to $12.75/$13.75.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended up 0.51 points at 72.85, a premium of 27.55 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index rose 2.65 points to 832.86.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 0.87 points at 91.26, premium of 2.57 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index added 9.50 points to 6,578.36.
